note: Phenotypic characterization across reported cohorts highlights a predominantly central neurodevelopmental and movement disorder phenotype without reports of primary severe polyneuropathy or episodic metabolic decompensation.

evidence.text: The core phenotype of ACBD6 deficiency across 45 patients comprises progressive neurodevelopmental delay, prominent dystonia/movement disorders, ataxia, spasticity, and midline brain anomalies, lacking reports of primary sensory-motor polyneuropathy, organomegaly, or recurrent ketoacidosis/hyperammonemia.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental ...
source.quote: The affected individuals (23 males and 22 females), aged 1-50 years, typically present with a complex and progressive disease involving moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) with significant expressive language impairment (98%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%) and mild cerebellar ataxia (85%) associated with gait impairment (94%), limb spasticity/hypertonia (76%), oculomotor (71%) and behavioural abnormalities (65%), overweight (59%), microcephaly (39%) and epilepsy (33%).

evidence.text: A case report described two siblings with biallelic ACBD6 variants developing morbid obesity, pancytopenia, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, representing rare systemic end-organ complications rather than acute episodic metabolic decompensation or severe peripheral polyneuropathy.

source.title: Neurodevelopmental Disorder, Obesity, Pancytopenia, Diabetes Mellitus, Cirrhosis, and Renal Failure in ACBD6-Associated Syndrome: A Case Report
source.quote: Clinical manifestations that have never been previously reported include morbid obesity, pancytopenia with severe infections, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, leading to deaths in their early 30s.
